The Prune

textContent.text: Clive the fruit fly flies over a vine. Kyle the fruit bat glides by. They both spot one ripe prune under a pine tree.
Clive dives first. "This prune is mine! Don't even try!" he cries.
Kyle lands softly. "That prune looks ripe. Just the way I like it."
Clive says, "Fine. Let's slice it and share."
"But we don't have a knife," says Kyle.
Clive pulls a twig from the pine. "This will do the trick!" he says. He tries and tries, but the twig just bends.
Kyle smiles. "Let's just try a bite."
Clive agrees.
They each take a bite. The prune is chewy and sweet. Clive grins. "This is quite nice."

The Magpie

textContent.text: "What a nice day!" Dad says. "Would you like to fly your kite?" he asks Giles. Giles nods, and they drive five miles to the sand dunes.
Giles unties the kite's string. He looks at the huge blue sky. "Let's give this a try," he thinks. Giles runs and the kite flies.
"Look! There's a magpie!" Dad yells. Giles spies the bird flying close to the kite. "Don't bite my kite," Giles cries. But the magpie just glides.
When the kite dives, the magpie dives too. "I think the magpie likes your kite," Dad says. They watch the kite and bird fly side by side.
"That is too cute," Giles says.

choices.text: He tells it to fly close to the sand.
He tells it not to bite his kite.
He tells it to fly next to his kite.

Sue the Fruit Fly

textContent.text: Sue the fruit fly rides her blue bike to June the mule's place. When June sees Sue on her bike, she is confused.
"Why didn't you just fly?" June asks Sue.
Sue lifts up a nice pie. "I made this for you to try!" she says. "I can't fly with pie."
June smiles. "That is so nice! I do not want to be rude, but what is inside this pie?"
Sue beams. "It is the best kind! Blueberry slime!"
June's eyes grow wide. She takes a step back. "Hmm. Next time can I have pie with no slime?"
Sue smiles. "Okay, this pie can be mine!" she says, and takes a bite.

textContent.text: "I want to make a slide for my mice," Luke tells his Mom.
They go to the shed and get some white tubes. They get a long blue tube too. "These are nice," Luke says. "The holes are a great size for mice!"
Luke uses the blue and white tubes to make a steep slide. He glues the tubes and paints them sky blue. He waits for them to dry.
After a while, Luke puts the slide inside the mice's cage.
The mice are shy, but soon they line up. They each slide on the tubes. Then, they run back to the top to ride again.
Luke smiles. "These mice like their slide!"

"I'd like some pie," Luke says. But Mr. Jules shakes his head. "No pie until the hive is clean," he says.
Luke's smile fades. This hive is twice the size of Luke's last one! He does not like the rule, but he goes away to clean. By the time he is done, Luke is tired.
He goes back to Mr. Jules. "What type of pie do we get today? Fruit pie?" he asks.
"No," Mr. Jules says, "Honey pie!"

textContent.text: "What a nice day!" Dad says. "Would you like to fly your kite?" he asks Giles. Giles nods, and they drive five miles to the sand dunes.
Giles unties the kite's string. He looks at the huge blue sky. "Let's give this a try," he thinks. Giles runs and the kite flies.
"Look! There's a magpie!" Dad yells. Giles spies the bird flying close to the kite. "Don't bite my kite," Giles cries. But the magpie just glides.
When the kite dives, the magpie dives too. "I think the magpie likes your kite," Dad says. They watch the kite and bird fly side by side.
"That is too cute," Giles says.
